Header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Diaz (Redwood SE), Lisa Patel (Evergreen CTO), Jordan Kim (Lead ML Eng), Avery Brooks (Platform Eng)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Quick hosted API demo focusing on streaming, parameters, and retry semantics. Customer interested in latency profile and security/compliance. Next steps agreed.

00:00 - Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, I'll hand it to Carlos for the demo in a minute.
01:20 - Carlos (Redwood SE): Cool, hi Lisa, Jordan, Avery. Today I'm going to show a short walk-through of Redwood's Hosted API for chat and text generation — streaming, common params, and how retries work. I'll jump into the Console and then a short SDK demo.
03:10 - Jordan (Evergreen): Quick Q — we care a lot about p50 at ~200ms for short turns, and also cost, so curious how streaming affects both.
05:00 - Carlos: Great question. Streaming lets you get partial tokens as they generate — it reduces end-user perceived latency because you can start rendering before the full completion. For per-token cost it's the same, but you can cut UI latency. In Console you can enable streaming via the route settings or in the SDK by using client.chat.stream().
07:00 - Avery: Which transport do you use? SSE? Websocket?
08:00 - Carlos: We support chunked HTTP (SSE-like) and also websocket for high-throughput low-latency use cases. The SDK abstracts it: node example uses EventSource under the hood, python uses an iterator. I'll paste the sample later.
09:10 - Maya: For quick context — Evergreen said pilot will be user-facing summarization inside their analytics product, so small results quickly are important.
11:00 - Lisa: Yes, exact. Also want to know about params — like temperature, top_p, max_tokens — and what defaults you recommend.
12:20 - Carlos: Defaults are tuned for balanced outputs. For deterministic summarization we recommend temp 0.0-0.2, top_p 0.8-0.95, and max_tokens sized to your summary length, obviously. Also show that stop sequences help you bound tokens. In Console we expose a slider and you can A/B test.
14:00 - Jordan: Do you have rate limits and how do retries interact? We use aggressive client-side retries now and want to avoid duplicates.
15:30 - Carlos: Redwood returns standard 429s for rate limits; our SDK includes exponential backoff. For idempotency you should set a request_id/idempotency_key header — if a retry happens and the server already accepted the request we return the previous result or a 409 depending on the operation. For streaming, if connection drops, the SDK will retry with the same idempotency key when safe.
17:00 - Avery: If we add an idempotency key, do we get dedup across multiple model variants?
18:00 - Carlos: Yes within the same deployment route, we dedup. If you change the pinned model version mid-flight, behavior depends on the route policy; typically dedup is per-route+key. We'll share docs.
20:00 - Maya: Let's flip to a short live demo. Carlos, screen share?
20:30 - Carlos: Sharing. I'm in the Console. Here's the Hosted API route config: model, max_tokens, streaming toggle, client rate limits, and fallback policy. I click into "Try it" — sending a chat prompt with streaming on.
22:00 - Carlos (streaming demo): You can see chunks coming in — partial tokens every ~50–150ms depending on model size. For short replies you see latency p50 ~180–250ms on our hosted smallest model; p95 higher.
24:00 - Jordan: Are the models Open weights or proprietary? Also do you host third-party models?
25:00 - Carlos: We offer a model catalog — both open models we license and Redwood-verified builds. For hosted API we serve validated model variants (quantized) for performance. If you need private model hosting, Dedicated or Private is the path.
26:20 - Lisa: Security questions — SOC2, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS integration, SSO?
27:30 - Maya: Yes — we have SOC2 (Type II), support customer-managed KMS, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC in Console, and audit logging. We'll attach the SOC2 report and a security brief.
29:00 - Avery: Data retention — can you opt out of retention for hosted?
30:00 - Maya: For hosted we offer configurable retention windows and stricter retention for enterprise plans; Private deployment gives full control and no telemetry leaves the VPC. We'll outline tradeoffs in the doc.
31:30 - Jordan: Back to performance — what about batching and caching — can Optimize help tune that for our workload?
32:30 - Carlos: Yes, Redwood Optimize will analyze your traffic patterns and recommend batching, KV/prefix caching and quantization profiles. That can reduce costs significantly while preserving latency SLOs. Console shows per-route token breakdown and cost estimates.
34:00 - Lisa: If we start with hosted and then move to Dedicated later, how seamless is it?
34:45 - Maya: It's designed to be seamless at the API layer — you can pin model versions per environment and update routing policies. Some infra differences (networking, SLAs) but developer experience remains the same.
35:30 - Jordan: Pricing? We have a tight budget for pilot — need rough numbers.
36:00 - Maya: I'll send the hosted pricing sheet and an example TCO that shows hosted vs dedicated for your expected qps. Also include a short benchmark script you can run.
37:00 - Maya: Quick recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2/security docs, streaming SDK samples, and schedule a benchmark next week. Any other questions?
37:30 - Lisa: No, that's it. Thanks — excited to try the sample.
37:50 - Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark.
38:00 - End of recording.
